identity.name: Microsoft 365 Storage Exfiltration + Mailbox Enumeration by an Azure Application (SIM-CLOUD-008)
identity.summary: An Azure AD OAuth app binds a MailItemsAccessed burst across many Exchange mailboxes (mailbox enumeration by an app), then drives a bulk OneDrive/SharePoint download burst (M365 storage exfiltration). Two XSIAM Analytics alerts fire on the unified audit log (msft_o365_audit); a correlation stitches enumeration to exfiltration on the shared identity into one incident.
identity.description: This card validates the two Microsoft 365 data-plane Analytics alerts a customer expects on the unified audit log when a compromised or over-consented OAuth application is used for collection and exfiltration: (1) 'Mailbox enumeration activity by Azure application' — an Azure AD app service principal performs a high-fan-out MailItemsAccessed Bind sweep across MANY distinct Exchange Online mailboxes, the app-driven mailbox-harvest shape (T1114); and (2) 'Microsoft 365 storage services exfiltration activity' — a bulk FileDownloaded / FileSyncDownloadedFull burst pulls sensitive documents out of OneDrive/SharePoint (T1567.002). Both are Cortex XSIAM Analytics alerts named in the XSIAM Analytics Alert Reference by data source (Azure Audit Log); neither keys on a known-bad string — the signal is the volume / object-diversity of the operation on the app or user identity in the msft_o365_audit dataset. There is deliberately no internal process-causality chain (the M365 unified-audit dataset carries no causality_actor_process_* fields), so these are Analytics detections, NOT ABIOCs — the cross-stage link forms on the shared identity, not a process tree. The scenario drives the m365_activity_emitter EAL plugin to POST shape-true O365 Management Activity API records (the unified audit log XSIAM ingests as msft_o365_audit) into an operator-supplied collector, so a DC can prove the alerts fire without touching a real tenant, reading a real mailbox, or downloading a real file. A correlation rule fuses the enumeration and exfiltration Analytics alerts on the shared UserId / ClientIP into a single collection-to-exfiltration incident, and two validation XQL queries confirm the emitted records actually landed in the dataset.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CLOUD-008 — m365_activity_emitter drives mailbox-enumeration-by-app then storage-exfiltration analytics into msft_o365_audit.

prerequisites.description: An HTTP log collector (XSIAM Broker VM HTTP applet / Cribl / nginx forwarder) is wired into Cortex XSIAM as a Microsoft 365 unified-audit source so POSTed records normalise into msft_o365_audit.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE: no real Microsoft 365 tenant is touched. The m365_activity_emitter
# EAL plugin POSTs shape-true O365 unified-audit records (msft_o365_audit) to an
# operator-supplied, allowlisted collector. See the SIM-CLOUD-008 scenario for the
# full campaign wiring; this payload documents the two-stage drive.
set -euo pipefail
COLLECTOR_URL="${COLLECTOR_URL:-https://xsiam-collector.cortexsim-canary.invalid/logs/v1/event}"
echo "[CortexSim] SIM-CLOUD-008 stage 1: mailbox enumeration by Azure app -> ${COLLECTOR_URL}"
echo "[CortexSim] SIM-CLOUD-008 stage 2: bulk OneDrive/SharePoint storage exfiltration -> ${COLLECTOR_URL}"
echo cortexsim-cloud-008-m365-enum-then-exfil-complete

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: Operator-supplied HTTP log collector wired into XSIAM as a Microsoft 365 unified-audit source.

expected_artifacts.description: A high-fan-out MailItemsAccessed Bind burst across many distinct mailboxes in the unified audit log attributed to one Azure AD application (AppId), the mailbox-enumeration-by-app shape.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: Workload = "Exchange" and Operation = "MailItemsAccessed" and MailAccessType = "Bind" and AppId != null

expected_artifacts.description: A bulk FileDownloaded / FileSyncDownloadedFull burst against OneDrive/SharePoint pulling sensitive documents out of the tenant, the storage-exfiltration shape.

xql_queries.name: Mailbox Enumeration Activity by an Azure Application
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter Workload = "Exchange" and Operation = "MailItemsAccessed"
| filter MailAccessType = "Bind" and AppId != null
| comp count() as bind_ops, count_distinct(ObjectId) as mailboxes_touched by AppId, ClientAppId, UserId, ClientIP
| filter bind_ops >= 20 and mailboxes_touched >= 5
| sort desc bind_ops
| fields AppId, ClientAppId, UserId, ClientIP, bind_ops, mailboxes_touched

xql_queries.name: Microsoft 365 Storage Services Exfiltration Activity
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter Workload in ("OneDrive", "SharePoint") and Operation in ("FileDownloaded", "FileSyncDownloadedFull")
| comp count() as download_ops, count_distinct(ObjectId) as files_pulled by UserId, ClientIP, Workload
| filter download_ops >= 15 and files_pulled >= 5
| sort desc download_ops
| fields UserId, ClientIP, Workload, download_ops, files_pulled

xql_queries.name: Mailbox Enumeration by Azure App Landed in Unified Audit Log
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter Operation = "MailItemsAccessed" and mailbox_enumeration_marker = true
| comp count() as bind_events, count_distinct(AppId) as apps by UserId, ClientIP, AppId
| filter bind_events >= 1
| sort desc bind_events
| fields UserId, ClientIP, AppId, bind_events, apps

xql_queries.name: Microsoft 365 Storage Exfiltration Download Burst Landed in Unified Audit Log
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_o365_audit
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter Operation in ("FileDownloaded", "FileSyncDownloadedFull") and storage_exfiltration_marker = true
| comp count() as download_events, count_distinct(ObjectId) as files by UserId, ClientIP
| filter download_events >= 1
| sort desc download_events
| fields UserId, ClientIP, download_events, files

correlation_rules.name: Microsoft 365 App-Driven Mailbox Enumeration to Storage Exfiltration Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: Analytics(Mailbox Enumeration Activity by an Azure Application) AND Analytics(Microsoft 365 Storage Services Exfiltration Activity) observed on the same UserId / ClientIP within the run window — stitches app-driven mailbox harvest (MailItemsAccessed Bind burst across many mailboxes) followed by a bulk OneDrive/SharePoint download burst into a SINGLE Microsoft 365 collection-to-exfiltration incident. The shared identity (the mailbox owner UPN and the client IP the OAuth app operates from) is the pivot; the incident's terminal assertion is that one actor enumerated mailboxes AND pulled bulk storage in the same window, distinguishing a genuine data-theft chain from an isolated noisy download.

threat_scenarios.name: Microsoft 365 App-Driven Mailbox Enumeration and Storage Exfiltration
threat_scenarios.description: Proves Cortex XSIAM fires its two Microsoft 365 data-plane behavioral analytics alerts — mailbox enumeration by an Azure application, and storage-services exfiltration — on the unified audit log (msft_o365_audit), and stitches them on the shared identity into one collection-to-exfiltration incident, all driven by shape-true synthetic audit records with no real tenant touched.

threat_steps.objective: The mailbox-enumeration-by-app Analytics alert fires on a high-fan-out MailItemsAccessed Bind sweep across many mailboxes attributed to one Azure AD application.
preconditions: An HTTP log collector wired into XSIAM as a Microsoft 365 unified-audit source (msft_o365_audit).
steps: Drive the m365_activity_emitter mailbox_enumeration_by_app pattern (fanned across >= 5 distinct mailbox UPNs) into the collector.
Observe the Analytics alert 'Mailbox enumeration activity by Azure application' fire.
Confirm the validation XQL shows the Bind burst landed in msft_o365_audit.
success_criteria: Analytics alert `Mailbox enumeration activity by Azure application` fires within the run window.
Validation XQL `Mailbox Enumeration by Azure App Landed in Unified Audit Log` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The storage-services-exfiltration Analytics alert fires on a bulk OneDrive/SharePoint FileDownloaded / FileSyncDownloadedFull burst.
steps: Drive the m365_activity_emitter storage_exfiltration pattern into the collector.
Observe the Analytics alert 'Microsoft 365 storage services exfiltration activity' fire.
Confirm the validation XQL shows the download burst landed in msft_o365_audit.
success_criteria: Analytics alert `Microsoft 365 storage services exfiltration activity` fires within the run window.
Validation XQL `Microsoft 365 Storage Exfiltration Download Burst Landed in Unified Audit Log` returns >= 1 row.

threat_steps.objective: The correlation stitches the enumeration and exfiltration Analytics alerts on the shared identity into one incident.
preconditions: TC-CLOUD-008A and TC-CLOUD-008B completed in the same run window on the same UserId / ClientIP.
steps: Run both emitter patterns for the same target_user against the same collector.
Observe CR-CLOUD-0008 raise one collection-to-exfiltration incident.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-CLOUD-0008` raises exactly one incident stitching both Analytics alerts on the shared UserId / ClientIP.

preventive_controls: Scope Azure AD (Entra) application permissions to least privilege and require admin approval for Mail.Read / Files.Read.All app-only grants; inventory consented apps and alert on new high-privilege grants.
Enforce Conditional Access and app-based Continuous Access Evaluation so a stolen app token cannot silently bind mailboxes or bulk-download storage from an anomalous client IP.
Apply DLP and download/throttling policies on OneDrive/SharePoint so a mass FileDownloaded burst is rate-limited and flagged.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune the two ABIOCs on per-application mailbox-access volume and per-identity storage-download volume/object-diversity rather than hand-authoring static thresholds.
Correlate app-driven mailbox enumeration with a subsequent bulk storage-download burst on the shared identity to promote a noisy single-alert into a collection-to-exfiltration incident.
Validate the msft_o365_audit ingestion path with the two landing XQL queries so a POV proves the unified-audit source is parsed before asserting the analytics fired.
